One of the World’s Priciest Mushrooms Is in Season Near Mt. Shasta Starting Today

Active NorCal Follow on Twitter September 16, 2026
Facebook Twitter Pinterest Reddit
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:29
Instaread

Somewhere under the pine duff around McCloud, one of the most valuable mushrooms on Earth is pushing up right now, and as of this morning it is legal to go dig it.

The 2026 matsutake harvest season opened Wednesday, September 16, on the Mount Shasta and McCloud ranger districts of the Shasta-Trinity National Forest, and it runs through November 30.

The opening comes with a catch. Personal-use permits do not exist for the fall matsutake season. Every picker needs a commercial permit, must be at least 18 with a valid ID, and has to keep a written log of picking dates and pounds harvested. Getting caught without paperwork, or with a permit and no log, can mean a citation. Forest Service officers patrol the harvest areas.

A four-day minimum runs $20 for up to 20 pounds, with each additional consecutive day another $5. A 30-day permit costs $100 for up to 100 pounds, and a full-season permit is $200 for 200 pounds. Permits from neighboring forests are not valid here.

Permits are sold at the McCloud Ranger Station on Forest Road (cash or check only, Fridays and Saturdays) and the Mt. Shasta Ranger Station at 204 W. Alma St. (cards accepted, Tuesday through Friday). Call (530) 964-2184 or (530) 926-4511.

Matsutake grow in a tight relationship with tree roots, which is why the permit forbids raking or disturbing the ground cover. Tear up the duff and the patch may not come back next year.
